deviations.what: The grid binds [attr.aria-labelledby]="labelledBy" and asks for label only when labelledBy is empty (HwValueControl.labelledBy: the application's aria-labelledby, else the label id of a surrounding hw-field)
deviations.why: Convention name-without-visible-label (NAME-05): inside an hw-field the control is named by the field label. Outside a field the rendered attributes are exactly those of the specified expression.

deviations.what: The text input also gets [attr.form]="form"; endEditing($event) emits (blurred)
deviations.why: HwValueControl.form is written on every native control; the text input carries the required and custom validity.
The template calls it; Angular templates cannot read private members.

deviations.what: dialogTemplate() lives in the new internal file src/dialog-template.ts, not in overlays.ts
deviations.why: public-api.ts re-exports everything from overlays.ts; a function exported there would become public API.

deviations.what: The shared cell fragments (tableCells, tableCell) live in the new internal file src/table-templates.ts and both tables interpolate them
deviations.why: One fallback template for both components without a public export.

deviations.what: Not asserted for Angular: a one-way [sortKey] is the initial state and the component then updates its own field
deviations.why: Convention controlled-and-observable-state: Angular has no controlled mode (the same exception step 1 records for RESET-05 and combobox STATE-02).
The navigation specification defines HwNamedRoot with the same expression and host bindings and says other clusters can extend it; the rendered attributes are those specified.

deviations.what: A menu that starts open ([open] on the first change) also gets its first enabled item as the active one, without taking focus; a later bound change to open sets the active item and focuses it after the render. The check uses a private record of the open state the component itself produced, so a [(open)] echo of the reader's own opening (ArrowUp on the trigger) does not move focus back to the first item.
deviations.why: endState.dom: exactly the active item has tabindex=0. Focus on the first render would steal focus at page load, and the two-way echo would otherwise override ArrowUp.
Convention angular-host-attributes: the inherited host binding removes aria-invalid from the wrapper, so the value is bound on the element that needs it (role tree supports aria-invalid).

deviations.what: The plain requirement is written @else {<ng-container>{{ requirement }}</ng-container>} and the loop declares let index = $index
deviations.why: The specified `@else {{{ requirement }}}` is three opening braces in a row, which the template parser does not read as a block followed by an interpolation.

deviations.what: As specified, Row extends Record<string, unknown>: a row type declared as an interface (no index signature) is not accepted by [rows], a type alias is
deviations.why: Recorded for the owner: `Row extends object` would accept interfaces too; the specified constraint was kept so that the four adapters agree.

deviations.what: (sortChange) cannot be a template error by itself: Angular treats an unknown event on a component element as a DOM event. The compile test reads $event.direction, which is the error an application that used the payload gets
deviations.why: Angular has no diagnostic for an unknown output.

deviations.what: A column `cell` that is not a TemplateRef is ignored and the row value is printed as text (cellTemplate() in table-templates.ts)
deviations.why: tests/table-parity.test.ts passes one column array with React-style cell functions to all adapters; a function reached ngTemplateOutlet and threw (templateRef.createEmbeddedViewImpl is not a function). The declared type stays TemplateRef.

deviations.what: Space on a focused a.hw-menu-item activates it (preventDefault, click)
deviations.why: Not stated in the specification: a button item is activated by Space natively, a link is not, and Space would scroll the page under the open menu. The other adapters should match or the owner may remove it.

deviations.item: tests listed under tests/*.test.ts and tests/browser/*.spec.ts
deviations.what: The Angular side of every listed case id is in packages/angular/test with the same ids (dates.test.ts, overlays.test.ts, disclosure-data.test.ts, tables.test.ts, stepper.test.ts, menus-tree.test.ts, portal-service.test.ts, required-names.test.ts, side-navigation.test.ts, renamed-inputs.test.ts, ssr.test.ts, hydration.test.ts); the root parity files and the browser suite were not edited
deviations.why: Only packages/angular/** is owned by this step.

deviations.what: The server-equals-client comparison of the dialog and accordion scenarios ignores what only a browser does after hydration: `open` on a dialog bound open, and the accordion motion attributes (data-hw-expanded, aria-expanded on the summary, inert / aria-hidden on collapsed content, the native name of an exclusive group). 'breadcrumb, pagination and stepper' is asserted on the server and hydrated in place, not compared, because a pagination inside a disabled fieldset is synchronised in the browser
deviations.why: These attributes are written by browser-only enhancements that already existed; none is part of this step.
